transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Well… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having some thoughts that are kind of hard to say out loud. Nothing I’ve acted on or planned, but I keep catching myself thinking maybe it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I don’t want to worry anyone, but… I figured I should probably talk to somebody about it.
How long have these thoughts been going on like this?

It’s been… a little while, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I haven’t made any kind of plan to hurt myself or anything like that. It’s more like I keep catching myself thinking, you know, maybe it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I figured I should say something before it got… I don’t know, more serious.
When did you first start having these thoughts about not waking up?

I… I’m not exactly sure when it first started. It’s been a little while, but it’s mostly just been these thoughts like, maybe it’d be easier if I didn’t wake up. I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself or anything, just to be clear. I know that probably sounds bad, but that’s why I thought I should come in and talk about it.
Can you think back and tell me if these thoughts of not waking up have been going on for more than two weeks?

I think… yes, probably more than two weeks. Not constant or anything, and I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself, but the thought keeps coming up that maybe it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I’m sorry, I know that’s not a great answer, but that’s the honest one.
Have you noticed that you don’t take as much pleasure or interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I guess I have noticed that some. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but the stuff that usually helps me unwind just hasn’t been doing much for me. Like fishing, looking through my records, tailgating… even checking on my home-brew. It’s more like I have to make myself do it, like it’s a chore instead of something I look forward to. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but after that burst of energy wore off, it felt like somebody just pulled the plug on me. Most days I’d end up sitting at the table, just staring at my coffee, feeling kind of empty… and ashamed, I guess. Does that count as depressed?
Have you noticed a loss of energy or felt more tired than usual nearly every day?

I’m not sure I’d say nearly every day, exactly. I mean, I’ve been tired, sure, but I don’t know if it’s more than what anybody would feel when things are off. Some days I can still get moving once I have to. So… maybe a little, but I’m not sure it’s a big thing. Does that answer it okay?
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty or like you’re not worth much lately?

I don’t know… not in a big way, I don’t think. I mean, I’ve had moments where I feel bad about myself or like I should be doing better, but I’m not walking around thinking I’m worthless all the time. It’s more just… I get frustrated with myself, if that makes sense. Is that kind of what you mean?
Have you noticed any trouble focusing or thinking clearly lately, like it’s harder to make decisions or stay focused on tasks?

I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I have normal moments where I lose my train of thought or put something off, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed a big problem making decisions or focusing. At work I can still do what I need to do, mostly. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently — like eating a lot more or a lot less than usual — nearly every day?

A little, yeah… I guess I haven’t been eating as much. Most days I kind of have to remind myself to eat, and by supper it just looks like too much trouble sometimes. My jeans are a bit looser, but I don’t want to make it sound dramatic or anything. Is that the sort of change you mean?
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling more restless or fidgety than before?

No, I don’t think I’ve noticed anything like that. I mean, I might get a little antsy here and there, like anybody, but not to where I’d say I’m pacing around or talking slower or anything. I think I’m moving pretty normal. Is that what you mean?
Can you tell me if most days, for most of the day, you’ve felt down or depressed?

Yeah… I guess I have, some days. I don’t want to overstate it, but after that big burst of energy kind of wore off, it was like somebody pulled the plug on me. I’d just sit at the kitchen table staring at my coffee, feeling… empty, and pretty ashamed of myself. Most of the day, yeah, it could feel that way. Is that what you mean?
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I hate to make it sound worse than it is, but after that burst of energy wore off, it really did feel like somebody pulled the plug on me. Most days I’d end up just sitting at the table, staring at my coffee, feeling kind of empty… and ashamed, I guess. So yes, for a couple weeks at least, it was most of the day.
